sdjwt-kid-not-iss.v1.txt.note: the attacker's key in kid, the victim's DID in iss, a valid key binding — the forgery A7-01 names

sdjwt-kid-self-iss-listed.v1.txt.note: a self-certifying kid beside a trust-listed iss

sdjwt-no-iss.v1.txt.note: no iss: there is no issuer to bind the key to

sdjwt-kid-fragment-ok.v1.txt.note: kid is iss with a fragment — it selects among the issuer's keys

sdjwt-listed-iss-ok.v1.txt.note: a listed issuer, its key found under iss alone

countersign-alias.v1.json.note: did:kash:X and did:kash:X#c are one key — one signer, no proof

countersign-requester-accepts.v1.json.note: the requester's own acceptance is a signature, never a countersignature; the independent one makes the proof

countersign-junk-sibling.v1.json.note: a sibling signature that is not base64 is skipped, not thrown

countersign-custody-missing.v1.json.note: no keyCustody stated: unknown, not subject-held

countersign-nonjson-subject.v1.json.note: a subject that is bytes, not JSON, is judged as bytes
